To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dietary supplementation with uridine 5'-monophosphat (UMP) increases acetylcholin (ACh) content and release in striatal extracellular space, and that this effect is observed in aged as well as young rats, suggesting that the effect is not age-related but rather due to the ability of UMP to increase brain levels of phosphatidyl-choline, a source of choline for ACh synthesis.

dietary uridine-5’-monophosphate, a precursor for phosphatidic acid synthesis, increases levels of acetylcholine and the acetylcholine increase caused by giving atro-pine in striatum of both young and aged rats.
oral administration of UMP to aged rats significantly increases striatal acetylcholine content and release, and enhances the atropine-evoked increase in striatal acetylcho-line release.

the role that dietary uridine plays in the biosynthesis of brain phospholipids, particularly in the aging process.
how the brain uses circulating precursors to synthesize membrane phospholipids.
the biosynthesis of membrane phosphatides in the brain and the role they may play in maintaining normal brain function.

dietary supplementation with uridine, or its membrane phosphatide precursors, can increase brain phosphatide and acetylcholine levels, and that these increases may be useful in the management of some neurological and psychiatric disorders.
